# v0.4.0 — Stronger experimental-method controls

This release strengthens the repository where a course can most easily teach the wrong lesson: basis choice, null ablations, and steering interventions.

## Highlights

- C10 demonstrates exact linear function preservation under a coordinated invertible basis change.
- C11 constructs a redundant-path counterexample where single ablations preserve accuracy while changing the logit margin.
- C12 requires dose response, sign reversal, equal-norm random directions, and an orthogonal control for steering claims.
- Every C01–C12 experiment now has a unique lab guide with predictions, metrics, modification tasks, and forbidden inferences.
- The representation and causal-methods chapters now connect these methodological cautions to runnable evidence.
- Advanced exercises train learners to downgrade conclusions to the level actually supported by the experiment.

The new experiments remain L0/L1 evidence. They establish exact identities or transparent counterexamples; they do not prove universal mechanisms in frontier models.
